evaluation: Final held-out test evaluation — Fusion-MIL, single clean run, no post-hoc tuning
model: Fusion-MIL (checkpoint: fusion_mil_final, trained on 127/150 slides, epoch 4, training val_auroc=0.9154)
test_set: 20 slides (8 tumor + 12 normal), genuinely never seen during training, validation, architecture selection, or hyperparameter tuning at any point in this project
key_finding: AUROC=0.927 on held-out test, consistent with (in fact slightly above) the 4-fold cross-validation range for Fusion-MIL (0.901-1.000, mean 0.966), confirming the CV results were not overfit to the validation folds. Precision and specificity are perfect (1.0) -- zero false positives across 12 normal slides. However sensitivity is only 0.75 -- 2 of 8 tumor slides were missed (false negatives). This precision/sensitivity trade-off is a genuine, honestly-reported limitation: the model is conservative and avoids false alarms, but at the cost of missing some malignant cases, which is clinically more costly than a false positive.
caveat: n=20 (8 tumor) is a small test set -- each misclassified slide moves sensitivity by 12.5 percentage points. This is a directional confirmation of the CV results, not a large-scale clinical validation. The model was selected and its checkpoint frozen before this evaluation was run, so no cherry-picking or tuning occurred based on this result.
